hot.title: An algebraic quantization of gravity from the null cone
hot.summary: Authors quantize gravity in a finite causal diamond by solving null-cone constraints and quantizing boundary data and a shear-sensitive clock. Shear delays reaching a fixed corner area, so a maximum clock reading selects a finite-dimensional sector. The trace yields the Bekenstein–Hawking area term and a one-loop logarithmic correction of 106/45 for a large Schwarzschild black hole at fixed mass, angular momenta summed.

hot.title: Recursive Collective Intelligence: Emergence on an Equal-Budget Ladder in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
hot.summary: The authors test when multi-agent communication adds value beyond independent attempts at equal token cost. On HiddenBench, fact forwarding among four Qwen3.8-27B agents reaches 0.959 accuracy, 0.310 above compute-matched pass@n; the full-information agent scores 0.942. On held-out SplitBench tasks, recursive training improves the group’s margin from −0.253 at G0 to +0.159 at G2. These findings are limited to the tested settings.

hot.title: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer
hot.summary: U-MoLT improves validation quality and enables single-traversal decoding with shared Transformer layers. Mixture-of-Loops Attention reads sequence key–value memory and selected same-token layer memory; loop-KV feedback uses only earlier-token positions, allowing each new token to reuse cached prefix memory. After 400B tokens, its 3B MoE model improves mean 10-domain perplexity from 13.99 to 13.24. S-size latency is comparable to OLMo3 in one tested setup.

hot.title: Agentic LongLive: Asynchronous Agentic Memory for Long Video Generation
hot.summary: Agentic LongLive adds an asynchronous memory agent to live video generation, preparing text and image memories from revealed prompts while each shot plays. The agent selects memories for the next shot without reading generated video or waiting for future prompts. On LongStory-Online, with the LongLive-2.0 generator and prompts fixed, state accuracy rose from 38.2% to 64.5%, identity from 44.1% to 89.0%, and revisit consistency from 15.0% to 55.4%; these are judge-scored rates on the tested benchmark.

hot.title: Reinforcement Learning Can Be Recovered From Its Own Rollouts
hot.summary: The authors test whether supervised learning on archived reinforcement-learning responses can recover online reinforcement-learning progress. Chronological maximum-likelihood replay trains on saved correct and incorrect responses without reward labels. On Qwen3-1.7B-Base, it tracks MaxRL across four benchmarks, with mean absolute pass@k gaps of 0.2–1.1 percentage points. Results depend on setting: late batches nearly recover some endpoints, but not universally.

hot.title: WeightSpaceBench: LLMs can't "feel" neural network weights (yet)
hot.summary: A family of benchmarks testing whether LLMs can read, fix and write neural network weights, with tools or from the weights alone. WSB-LM and WSB-Backdoor are the first two.

hot.title: OmniAct: One Policy, One Million Embodiments
hot.summary: OmniAct conditions a shared policy on each arm’s camera-relative joint geometry and predicts actions for its joints. In 2,000 simulated episodes with held-out embodiments and scenes, it achieves 63.0% success across six tasks at a 500-step cap, versus 57.9% for UMI all-views. Zero-shot, it succeeds in 13 of 20 OpenYAM setups, versus 7 for a baseline; evidence covers one arm and pick-and-place.

hot.title: AnyCam: Anything Can Represent Camera for Video Generation
hot.summary: AnyCam controls generated-video camera motion by reconstructing a user-selected object in 3D and rendering it along a target path. The video model uses these views as an object-relative reference while taking appearance and motion from the source. On DAVIS, normalized translation error is 0.028 versus 0.057 for a matched Plücker-ray baseline; poses are estimated from generated video, and anchors are not guaranteed suitable.

hot.title: Stable Gated DeltaNet-2: Understanding and Mitigating Recurrent State Instability
hot.summary: Stable GDN-2 stabilizes recurrent linear attention for long-context language models by aligning the directions used to read and erase stored associations, adding a decay-regulated residual write. Under stated assumptions, erasure is non-expansive without new writes. In roughly 1.60B-parameter recurrent models pretrained at 64K, it scores 11.62 on RULER at 128K, versus 4.82 for GDN-2; this is the overall recurrent average, not every setting.

hot.title: Sage-Med: Scaling Medical Multimodal Intelligence
hot.summary: Sage-Med is a 35-billion-parameter medical multimodal model trained with stage-specific data curation, medical pretraining, three supervised fine-tuning stages, and adaptive reinforcement learning. The authors report a 58.26% equal-weight average across 31 public multimodal benchmarks, compared with 52.24% for its base model. These benchmark results do not establish clinical benefit or formal scaling laws.

hot.title: Toward Agentic Robotics: A Large-Scale Study of Harness Design for Robot-Use Agents
hot.summary: X-Harness connects a vision-language model (VLM) to robot control through feedback-aware code that can use perception tools, motion primitives, or a vision-language-action (VLA) policy. The authors evaluate it across simulation benchmarks and model families without updating model weights. On LIBERO-PRO, Opus-written code reaches 95.4% success versus 58.6% for the matched VLA alone, but does not improve standard LIBERO.

hot.title: Verifiable On-Policy Distillation
hot.summary: The authors introduce Verifiable On-Policy Distillation (VOPD) for mathematical reasoning, using teacher–verifier agreement within groups of sampled responses to scale teacher guidance across next-token choices. VOPD compares teacher preferences with verified outcomes through a reference-model log-probability shift. In tests of two Qwen3 configurations and eight math benchmarks, it averages 66.38, above OPD and ExOPD, using the student’s top 16 tokens.

hot.title: Monitoring the Paper Machine: AI Research in the Age of Acceleration
hot.summary: The authors build an observatory tracking AI research output and public traces from papers and repositories across 11 venues. It analyzes paper text, GitHub histories, and closed-model dependencies to assess how research is produced and whether evidence remains checkable. In 2025, 14.3% of papers at five venues depended on models announced for retirement; the measures do not show AI caused growth.

hot.title: RoboEvo$^2$: Recursive Robot Self-Improvement via Harness-Policy Co-Evolution
hot.summary: RoboEvo² links a robot policy and repair harness, reusing verified corrections as skills and policy training data. In eight LIBERO-PRO settings, π₀.₅ standalone success rises from 11.0% to 84.1% and hybrid success from 30.4% to 90.5% over eight rounds, while per-round coding-agent API cost falls from $430.63 to $98.92. It starts from demonstrations and uses fixed skills and perception tools.

hot.title: Can image generation help visual reasoning? An empirical study
hot.summary: The authors test whether generated helper images improve visual question answering. A model writes a hint, an image generator creates a helper from the original image, and the model answers using both. Across 13 modular model–generator pairs, accuracy drops in 106 of 130 pair-by-task comparisons, averaging 3.7 percentage points across nine of ten tasks, with exceptions.

hot.title: Attention Latent Feedback
hot.summary: ALF (Attention Latent Feedback) lets each sublayer use the previous token’s outputs at its own and deeper layers, alongside a projected summary of the previous final state. Across three tested MoE sizes, it lowers held-out loss versus standard residual and final-state feedback. On MoE-4.0B, the four-domain average accuracy rises from 45.1% to 47.0% under teacher-forced scoring, not open-ended generation.

hot.title: EgoUseBench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents under Evolving First-Person Contexts
hot.summary: EgoUseBench introduces a benchmark for testing whether agents can connect first-person observations and user requests to website actions. It compares six models across Computer-Use, Offline Ego Use, and Online Ego Use settings using tasks and final-state success. Mean success rates are 86.1%, 64.2%, and 63.4%, respectively; these results show a gap between tested settings, not that evolving context alone causes it.

hot.title: DRBench Pro: A Knowledge-Centric Benchmark for Professional Deep Research Agents
hot.summary: The authors introduce a benchmark that measures how deeply and broadly deep-research reports cover a shared knowledge tree. It builds Wikipedia-derived reference trees and scores coverage across connected research directions and knowledge chains. Across 144 cases, Claude Opus 5 leads, with 57.04% overall coverage. These are rubric-based structural scores, not measures of all facts or overall report quality.

hot.title: WebVibe: Multimodal Interactive Website Generation via Reverse Synthesis and Visual Self-Distillation
hot.summary: WebVibe and Interactive-SDPO train models for interactive multi-page website generation. WebVibe builds sites, verifies navigation and widget behavior in a browser, then derives training descriptions from passing sites. Interactive-SDPO adds replay traces and before-and-after screenshots to feedback-conditioned training. On Vision2Web L2, InteractiveCoder-9B reaches 55.15 FS versus 20.20 for its base; controlled ablations support the combined recipe, not either component alone.

hot.title: EmbodiSafety: Benchmarking Risk Understanding and Response in Embodied AI
hot.summary: EmbodiSafety evaluates robot decisions in single-image Snapshot and ordered-frame Trajectory tasks across 1,632 decisions in 844 visual scenarios. It scores response mode, risk or uncertainty identification, and valid next action; Trajectory also tests recovery versus human escalation. Claude-Opus-5.5 leads reference models at 56.1% and 61.5% L3, measuring judged responses to generated scenes, not physical execution.

likes.title: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer
likes.summary: GLM-5.4 is Z.ai's first flagship model built on a Loop Transformer, which runs a weight-shared block of layers for multiple iterations to add reasoning depth without adding parameters. Rather than pre-training a looped model from scratch, Z.ai adapted the pre-trained GLM-5 base through continued training, looping 28 layers for two iterations at 750B scale. The post frames the model as the start of "Generalized Coding", where code generation extends to video, CAD, games, and 3D.

likes.title: Sample-Efficient In-Context Adaptation via Sleep
likes.summary: Sleep lets Transformer models refine their key-value cache at chunk boundaries, using recurrent passes over context already read. Rather than add depth to every generated token, the model updates its attention memory periodically, then resumes ordinary decoding. On held-out code, 1.2B-parameter models matched baseline loss with 2.10× fewer context tokens at N=2 and 2.39× at N=4; this measures prefix length, not speed.

likes.title: Language Model Harnesses can be Compositional Generalizers
likes.summary: The authors train an RLM harness using synthetic traces to improve transfer from shorter tasks to longer contexts. It keeps context outside the root prompt and uses programmatic calls to divide work among smaller inputs. In the same harness, fine-tuned Qwen3.8-27B reaches an eight-benchmark average of 58.5, versus 46.1 for the untrained model, with roughly half inference tokens; transfer is conditional.

likes.title: RoboUniverse-10K: Toward the Scaling Era of Agentic Robotics via Real-to-Sim Environments
likes.summary: RoboUniverse-10K turns real manipulation videos into simulated robot-training tasks by having coding agents build scenes, controllers, and verifiers, with an independent agent checking environments. Its 10,807 environments include 10,307 training tasks and 500 held-out tasks. GPT-6.2 Astra reaches 85.8% success on the held-out set, while simulated scenes remain simplified and tasks mostly short-horizon.

likes.summary: LoopRes lets pretrained language models reuse layers for additional computation by giving each reused layer access to recent intermediate results, with cues for their loop positions. On Qwen3-1.7B-Base, it scores 55.8 across seven math and code benchmarks at twice the compute per token of unlooped SFT, versus 43.2 for SFT; general-purpose performance remains untested.

likes.title: Pruning Autonomous Driving VLAs: What to Preserve for Reasoning and Action
likes.summary: MoOP compresses Alpamayo-1.5-10B by pruning a vision-language model (VLM) for both Chain-of-Causation explanations and trajectory generation. It ranks units using cross-entropy and flow-matching objectives, retaining VLM units important to either, and selects action-expert MLP channels across denoising steps. With VLM-only pruning at 24.0% total parameter reduction, it scores 68.8% on LingoQA versus 37.0% for FM-only; the dense model scores 73.2%, a difference from MoOP that is not statistically significant.

likes.title: From Interaction History to User Understanding: A Memory Architecture for Lifelong Agents
likes.summary: MUSE-Mem separates three decisions: what to retain, how evidence updates durable user knowledge, and when a query needs more detail. It links compact semantic memory to episodic sources, retrieving them only when requirements remain unsupported. On LongMemEval, it scores 87.20% versus Memora’s 82.60%, with 6.2k versus 8.2k answer-time memory tokens under Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite; findings are limited to benchmarks and setup.

likes.title: Weight-Space Programming of JEPA World Models
likes.summary: The authors test whether an LLM can edit a world model from a description of changed physics, without new-system data or gradients. In two simulations, edits remap changed controls into controls the model understands, improving predictions and sometimes planning. On Push-T gain 20→60, error falls 90%, from 0.529 to 0.054; object-dynamics changes remain difficult, and prediction gains do not always improve planning.

likes.title: Self-WSP: Can Language Models Improve Themselves Through Weight-Space Programming?
likes.summary: The authors introduce Self-WSP, in which a language model proposes edits to its weights, then solves questions with the edited model. An outer loop tests proposals on practice questions and selects runs by validation. On GSM8K, the selected model reaches 61.0% test accuracy, up from 11.8%; this is a result from one model, not evidence of reliable self-improvement.

likes.title: RoboInF: A Benchmark for Instruction Fidelity in Robotic Manipulation
likes.summary: RoboInF benchmarks whether manipulation policies follow instructions, not just reach task goals. It tests branches from the same scene and robot state, checking goals and constraints such as order and contact. For π₀.₅ post-trained on clear demonstrations, the eight-task average is 79.3% task success but 52.4% joint success, a 26.9-point gap; this is a simulation benchmark result, not evidence about real-world performance.
